A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SV4D work, with readable text, figures, equations, and tables. V1 ends with references despite mentioning an appendix; v2 supplies Appendices A-D. The supplied content supports comparison, although added documentation does not establish changes to previously undocumented implementation.

before.justification: V1 reports original novel-view synthesis and 4D reconstruction experiments, sampling ablations, and two user studies in Section 4.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and user studies and adds architecture ablations and per-view analysis in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The main attention architecture, mixed sampling, and dynamic-NeRF procedure match. V1's proposed spatio-temporal classifier-free guidance schedule disappears, while v2 newly documents skip connections and blending weights. The PDFs do not establish whether the implemented procedure changed or only its documentation.

E1.justification: Both versions use ObjaverseDy for training and retain ObjaverseDy, Consistent4D, and DAVIS evaluations for novel-view video synthesis and 4D generation. The added ablations and visual examples do not establish new dataset, domain, or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds 4Diffusion to the Consistent4D comparisons in Tables 1-2 and replaces the SV3D-based Diffusion2 reproduction with results attributed to official code. The anchor-only control disappears from Table 6, although anchor-frame comparisons remain in Table 5. Other comparator membership is retained.

E3.justification: The new 4Diffusion comparison uses its eight-frame outputs and excludes FVD-F because frame counts differ. Table 7 adds controlled architecture variants. Existing SV4D training budgets, principal metrics, and user-study procedures remain unchanged; newly specified resolution and sampler settings are disclosures rather than established setting changes.

E4.justification: V1 primarily analyzes anchor quality and sampling strategies. V2 substantially extends this to reference-view and conditioning ablations in Table 7 and view-specific temporal consistency in Figure 13. The no-frame-attention row numerically matches the existing SV3D row, whereas the other conditioning-ablation rows add distinct evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. User-study participant counts remain unspecified, and the added results use the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds 4Diffusion, conditioning-ablation, and per-view results. Diffusion2's ObjaverseDy FV4D changes from 977.19 to 1320.29 with the implementation-source change, not a demonstrated same-setting regression. Table 2 changes Efficient4D LPIPS from 0.140 to 0.130 and 4DGen from 0.130 to 0.140. Table 6 drops anchor-only LPIPS 0.130, while its FVD scores remain in Table 5. Existing SV4D benchmark scores and user-study preferences are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds explicit mathematical definitions of depth and image-gradient-weighted normal regularizers that v1 describes verbally. Appendix A.4 largely formalizes the existing attention operations. No new theorem, proof, or formal problem formulation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: unified frame/view generation, mixed sampling for long videos, efficient reconstruction without SDS, and state-of-the-art synthesis and 4D generation. Added evidence does not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: The sampling motivation changes from autoregressive error propagation to inconsistency between independently generated submatrices. V2 also explains attention blending and sequential attention tradeoffs, interprets the conditioning ablations, and qualifies comparisons through FVD's sensitivity to frame count.

D1.justification: Appendices A and C supply substantial information absent from v1: rendering and camera sampling, cached embeddings, the 21-view/21-frame training pool, 576-by-576 resolution, 50-step DDIM sampling, anchor indices, inference time, attention reshaping, reconstruction losses, learning rate, and baseline-result provenance. These are primarily documentation additions; the guidance-schedule explanation is removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning against concurrent work, including EG4D, Diffusion4D, Vivid-ZOO, and 4Diffusion. Beyond v1's emphasis on inference-only alternatives, v2 distinguishes SV4D through full-network fine-tuning and mixed sampling relative to other trained 4D models.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the section sequence remain intact. V2 makes local explanatory revisions, expands related work, organizes new material into Appendices A-D, changes to author-year citations, and removes the acknowledgments and guidance paragraph. The retained narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 2 to expose residual connections and adds sampling diagrams, visual comparisons, a per-view plot, and Table 7. It also relocates existing tables, revises Table 6's structure, and adopts the conference layout. These substantially expand the visual explanation and presentation of evidence.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens reproducibility and architectural validation: Appendices A and C supply previously absent implementation details and baseline provenance, while Table 7 and Figure 13 examine conditioning choices and view-dependent quality. Updated baseline evaluation also improves the comparison's relevance. These gains outweigh the lost guidance explanation; they do not indicate improved performance of the retained SV4D model.
